title: Composition and flatness for admissible module strict transforms
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, $f:X\to S$ a morphism, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. (1) For a $U$-admissible blowup $b:S_1\to S$ with centre $Z$ and a $b^{-1}(U)$-admissible blowup $c:S_2\to S_1$ with centre $Z_1$, there is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal on $S$ with zero set $Z\cup b(Z_1)$ whose blowup is isomorphic to $bc$ over $S$. Under this identification the strict transform of $\mathcal F$ along $bc$ is canonically isomorphic to its successive module strict transforms along $b$ and $c$, as modules on $X\times_SS_2$. (2) For any such $b$, if $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$, its strict transform is its ordinary pullback to $X\times_SS_1$ and is flat over $S_1$. In general the strict transform is quasi-coherent, is a quotient of this pullback, and agrees with $\mathcal F$ over $U$; it is of finite type if $\mathcal F$ is. The base $S_1$ is again quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Admissible blowups, centres and module strict transform are as in [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform]; module pullback is as in [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Write $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J$ for the finite-type quasi-coherent centre ideals retained by the admissibility data [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], $b$ is proper. Thus it is quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], hence quasi-separated [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Since $S$ is qcqs, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] gives that $S_1$ is qcqs, proving the last assertion of (2).

source.place: Tag 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective (properness); the qcqs consequence used in Tag 080Y, flat.tex remark-successive-blowups.

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-composition-of-blowups], in its current blueprint_update statement, to $S$, $\mathcal I$ and the centre $Z_1=V(\mathcal J)$ on $S_1$. Its hypotheses are satisfied because $S$ is qcqs and both centre ideals are finite type. It gives a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$ and an isomorphism $S_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)$ over $S$ with $V(\mathcal K)=Z\cup b(Z_1)$. Since $Z\cap U=\varnothing$ and $Z_1\cap b^{-1}(U)=\varnothing$, this union is disjoint from $U$. Consequently $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$: at every point of $U$ some local generator of $\mathcal K$ is a unit. Thus this specified composite blowup is $U$-admissible by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup].

source.place: Tag 080B, lemma-composition-finite-type-blowups; Tag 080K, definition-admissible-blowup; Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups.

proof.text: Set $X_i=X\times_S S_i$, with projections $p:X_1\to X$ and $q:X_2\to X_1$, using the associative fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\mathcal F_1$ be the first module strict transform, $\mathcal F_2$ its strict transform along $c$, and $\mathcal G$ the strict transform of $\mathcal F$ for the centre $\mathcal K$. The kernel lemma [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] makes $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_2$ quasi-coherent and gives epimorphisms $p^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F_1$ and $q^*\mathcal F_1\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F_2$. Pullback of the first epimorphism is an epimorphism: on stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] identifies it with tensoring the first epimorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] gives the surjectivity of the original stalk maps, and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] preserves this surjectivity. The stalk criterion of the same exactness node then gives the desired epimorphism of sheaves. Together with $(pq)^*\cong q^*p^*$ from [def-pc-module-pullback], this gives an epimorphism $H=(pq)^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F_2$. There is also the canonical epimorphism $H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G$ from the same kernel lemma.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups (1), first paragraph of proof; tensor right exactness in algebra.tex.

proof.text: Let $D\subset X_2$ be the inverse image of $V(\mathcal K)$, and let $L$ be the kernel of $H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F_2$. Off the inverse image of $Z$, the first quotient is an isomorphism by [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel]; off the inverse image of $Z_1$, the second is an isomorphism. Hence $L$ is supported on their union, which is contained in $D$ by step 2. The kernel $K$ of $H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G$ is precisely the subsheaf of sections supported on $D$, by that same lemma for the blowup with centre $\mathcal K$. Thus $L\subseteq K$ and quotienting gives a canonical epimorphism $\mathcal F_2=H/L\twoheadrightarrow H/K=\mathcal G$. Its kernel is supported on $D$.

source.place: Tag 080I, proof, the support argument and the factorization through the second strict transform.

proof.text: By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], $E=b^{-1}(Z)$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $S_1$. The first strict transform $\mathcal F_1$ has no nonzero local sections supported on the inverse image of $E$, by [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel]. Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-different-centers] on $S_1$ to the module $\mathcal F_1$ on $X_1$, the centre $Z_1$, and the Cartier divisor $E$. The product ideal $\mathcal J\mathcal I_E$ is finite type: locally $\mathcal J$ has finitely many generators and $\mathcal I_E$ has one. Under the isomorphism of blowups provided by [lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor], it identifies $\mathcal F_2$ with the strict transform for this product centre. By the kernel lemma for that centre, $\mathcal F_2$ therefore has no nonzero local sections supported on the inverse image of $Z_1\cup E$.

source.place: Tag 080I, final paragraph of proof; Tag 080H (2), lemma-strict-transform-different-centers; Tag 02OS, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor.

proof.text: The inverse image of $Z_1\cup E$ in $S_2$ equals $(bc)^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$. Indeed, over $S\setminus Z$, [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] applied with preserved open $S\setminus Z$ identifies $b$ with the identity, so a point there lies above $b(Z_1)$ exactly when its image in $S_1$ lies in $Z_1$. Above $Z$, both unions already contain every point, through $E$. The cited open is quasi-compact because on each affine in a finite cover of $S$ it is a finite union of principal opens, using the finite type of $\mathcal I$. Pulling the equality back to $X_2$ identifies the support set of step 5 with $D$. Therefore the kernel of $\mathcal F_2\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G$ from step 4 is zero, and the map is an isomorphism. It is characterized by its composite with the epimorphism $H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F_2$, so it is canonical and agrees with the specified identification of the ambient fibre products.

source.place: Tag 080I, conclusion of the proof of (1), and Tag 02OS (1).

proof.text: For any of the admissible blowups in (2), [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] gives the quasi-coherent quotient $p^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F^b$, and identifies it with $p^*\mathcal F$ away from the inverse image of $Z$. Since the admissible centre misses $U$, this includes the entire inverse image of $U$. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], the blowup restricted over $U$ is an isomorphism. Hence the restriction of $\mathcal F^b$ there identifies with the original restriction of $\mathcal F$, with its canonical pullback interpretation [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1) and its preceding paragraph; Tag 02OS (1).

proof.text: If $\mathcal F$ is of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type] makes $p^*\mathcal F$ finite type. Locally compose its surjection from a finite free module with the quotient map $p^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F^b$ from [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel]. The composite is still surjective, so $\mathcal F^b$ is finite type by [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Tag 080D (1), definition-strict-transform; finite type as in Modules Tag 01B5.

proof.text: Now assume $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$. Apply the module theorem [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback] to the base change $S_1\to S$, with no flatness assumption on this map or on $X\to S$. It makes $H_1=p^*\mathcal F$ flat over $S_1$; it is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. To prove that its strict-transform quotient is itself, it remains to show that $H_1$ has no nonzero local sections supported on the inverse image of $E$, where $E$ is the effective Cartier divisor supplied by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center].

source.place: Tag 080F (2), lemma-strict-transform-flat; module base change as in morphisms.tex Tag 01U4 and algebra.tex Tag 051D.

proof.text: Work on an affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S_1$ where $E$ is cut out by a nonzerodivisor $a\in A$, and an affine $V\subset X_1$ mapping into $W$. Put $N=H_1(V)$; by [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], $N$ is flat over $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the injective map $A\xrightarrow{a}A$: after tensoring with $N$ it says that multiplication by $a$ on $N$ is injective, hence so is multiplication by $a^n$ for every $n\geq0$. A section $t\in N$ supported on the inverse image of $E$ restricts to zero on $D(a)$ in $V$; clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-basic-open-localization], applied to the image of $a$ in $\mathcal O_{X_1}(V)$, gives $a^nt=0$ for some $n$. Thus $t=0$. Such affines cover $X_1$, so all local supported sections vanish. By [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel], the kernel of $H_1\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F^b$ is zero. Consequently $\mathcal F^b\cong p^*\mathcal F$, and the flatness of $H_1$ from step 9 proves the remaining flatness assertion.

source.place: Tag 080F (2), proof: vanishing of exceptional power torsion; algebra.tex Tag 00HD for flat tensor exactness and Properties Tag 07ZP for supported sections.
